name: La Pagode (Palais des Rois Bell)
description: Historic residence of the Bell royal dynasty in Bonanjo, built in the early 1900s. Often called La Pagode, it is one of Douala’s most iconic monuments and a symbol of Sawa heritage.
cost_note: Exterior visit free; budget for taxi and snack

tips.hours: Best viewed daytime; exterior accessible most days. Interior access varies — ask on site or at doual'art nearby.
tips.transport: Bonanjo is walkable once you are there. From Akwa: short taxi or moto (~500–1000 FCFA). Agree the price before you start.
tips.timing: Go early morning (8–10h) for better light and fewer cars around Place du Gouvernement.
tips.safety: Stay on main streets in Bonanjo. Keep phone and cash discreet. Avoid flashing valuables near busy corners.

name: Musée Maritime de Douala
description: National maritime museum in Bonanjo telling the story of Cameroon’s coastal peoples, trade, pirogues and the port of Douala. A top cultural stop for visitors.

tips.hours: Typically Tue–Fri ~9h–17h30; weekends often open later morning. Closed Mondays on many schedules — confirm before you go.
tips.transport: Rue de l’Hôpital, Bonanjo. Taxi from Akwa or Deido is straightforward; moto works if you know the area.
tips.timing: Weekday mornings are quieter. Combine with Parc Bonanjo and La Pagode the same half-day.
tips.safety: Official site with staff. Phone photos may need a small extra fee — ask at the desk.

name: Cathédrale Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul
description: Landmark Catholic cathedral with twin towers, completed in the 1930s. An important religious and architectural site in central Douala.

tips.hours: Open for visits outside mass times; Sunday mornings are for worship — be respectful if services are on.
tips.transport: Central Bonanjo / near Collège Libermann area. Walk from Place du Gouvernement if you are already on a heritage route.
tips.timing: Late morning or late afternoon for exterior photos; avoid blocking entrances during mass.
tips.safety: Calm area by day. Dress modestly if you enter. Do not leave bags unattended.

name: La Nouvelle Liberté
description: Famous recycled-metal sculpture by Joseph-Francis Sumégné at the Deido roundabout. A modern art landmark expressing freedom and urban creativity.

tips.hours: Outdoor monument — visible 24/7. Best light morning or late afternoon.
tips.transport: Rond-point Deido — heavy traffic. Taxi is safer than standing in the middle. Moto can drop you on the sidewalk side.
tips.timing: Go early to avoid peak traffic and for cleaner photos. Do not stop the car in the roundabout.
tips.safety: Very busy junction. Stay on the pavement; watch for motos on the sidewalk. Keep phones secure while shooting.

name: Parc Bonanjo
description: Green park in the heart of the administrative district. Ideal for a short walk, photos, and a break near Place du Gouvernement and nearby monuments.

tips.hours: Daytime use is best; treat it as a short break between Bonanjo sights.
tips.transport: Walk from La Pagode / Place du Gouvernement — no need for another taxi if you are already in Bonanjo.
tips.timing: Mid-morning shade is pleasant. After heavy rain, paths can be wet.
tips.safety: Fine by day with other visitors. Avoid isolated corners after dark.

name: Palais Dika Akwa
description: Striking palace built by Prince Dika Akwa in Akwa. Showcases Sawa architecture and is a notable heritage stop in the business district.

tips.hours: Exterior is the main tourist view; interior access is not always public — check locally.
tips.transport: Akwa — taxi or moto from Bonanjo is a short hop. Boulevard de la République area is busy.
tips.timing: Daytime for photos. Combine with an Akwa evening if you want food after.
tips.safety: Busy commercial zone. Use licensed taxis at night; agree fares first.

name: Doual'art
description: Contemporary art centre linked to La Pagode area. Exhibitions, public art projects, and a window into Douala’s creative scene.
cost_note: Exhibitions often free or low fee

tips.hours: Check exhibition days — not every day is open like a big museum. Linked to the Pagode / Bonanjo cultural circuit.
tips.transport: Same Bonanjo cluster as La Pagode — walk between stops.
tips.timing: Pair with La Pagode the same morning.
tips.safety: Cultural venue area is generally fine by day. Ask staff about current shows.

name: Place du Gouvernement
description: Historic square in Bonanjo surrounded by colonial-era buildings, close to La Pagode, the park, and memorials. Best explored on foot.

tips.hours: Open public space — daytime visits recommended.
tips.transport: Heart of Bonanjo. Start or end your heritage walk here.
tips.timing: Early morning for cooler air and fewer vehicles.
tips.safety: Stay aware of traffic when crossing. Standard city caution with bags.

name: Akwa District
description: Lively commercial and nightlife heart of Douala. Shopping, street food, hotels, and the pulse of the economic capital after dark.
cost_note: Food, drinks, local transport for an evening out

tips.hours: Shops by day; nightlife from evening. Food stands stay busy late.
tips.transport: Central hub — taxis and motos everywhere. At night prefer a known taxi or ride from your hotel.
tips.timing: Evening for atmosphere; daytime for shopping without the crush.
tips.safety: Busy and generally animated. Keep wallets front-pocket, avoid isolated side streets late, and fix moto/taxi prices before boarding.

name: Marché Central Mboppi
description: One of Central Africa’s largest markets. Spices, fabrics, electronics, and daily life — intense, colourful, and very Douala.

tips.hours: Peak activity morning to mid-afternoon. Many stalls wind down toward evening.
tips.transport: Taxi or moto; the area is congested. Know your exit point before you dive in.
tips.timing: Go with a clear list — it is easy to get overwhelmed. Morning is less humid than afternoon.
tips.safety: Crowded — bags in front, minimal jewellery. Negotiate calmly; walk away if pressure feels wrong.

name: Youpwe
description: Traditional fishing neighbourhood by the water. Fresh fish market, pirogues, and a glimpse of Douala’s coastal working life.

tips.hours: Fish market is liveliest in the morning when the catch arrives.
tips.transport: Taxi from Bonanjo/Akwa; ask for Youpwe / the fishing quarter. Moto is possible but roads can be rough.
tips.timing: Morning for market energy; lunch for grilled fish. Footwear that can handle wet ground helps.
tips.safety: Working waterfront — watch your step near pirogues. Ask before photographing people closely. Keep valuables secure.

name: Bonanjo Heritage Walk
description: Self-guided stroll through Douala’s administrative quarter: colonial façades, monuments, palm avenues, and the densest cluster of tourist sights in the city.
cost_note: Taxi + water/snack for a half-day walk

tips.hours: Best as a 2–3 hour daytime circuit (Pagode → Place → Parc → Cathedral → Maritime Museum).
tips.transport: Arrive by taxi to Bonanjo, then walk. Carry small notes for water and a return taxi.
tips.timing: Start before 10h — heat and traffic rise fast. Rainy season: pack a light poncho.
tips.safety: Stick to main administrative streets. Share your rough plan with someone; daytime walking is the norm for visitors.
